note: Bay water levels the explorer offers. All are still water (no waves) in feet NAVD88 unless 'waves' says otherwise. 'category' is the provenance: sourced = stated in the source; derived = arithmetic on sourced values; inference = our reading of an unclear source; sensitivity = a hypothetical combination with no established likelihood. Rows cite SOURCE_NOTES. 'precision' is the number of decimals shown where a finer figure would claim more than the source supports.

scenarios.label: Sensitivity test: king tide plus 1 ft (El Niño)
scenarios.source: 7.4 (W14) plus 1.0 ft, the upper end of the 6 to 12 inches a strong El Niño can add to sea level for several months (California Coastal Commission 2024 guidance, App. A; SOURCE_NOTES W15, H3). A hypothetical combination: how likely a king tide is to coincide with that increase is not established, and predicted tides leave out weather and El Niño (W14).

scenarios.label: Sensitivity test: 10-year storm tide plus 1 ft (El Niño)
scenarios.source: 8.47 (W11) plus 1.0 ft (W15, H3). A hypothetical combination with no established return period: the extreme-tide statistics are fitted to a 1973–2003 record that includes the 1977–78, 1982–83 and 1997–98 El Niño winters, so part of the 1 ft is counted twice (W16).

scenarios.label: A 12 ft level quoted at a Council committee (Oct 22, 2026)
scenarios.source: Scott Ferris, Budget and Finance Policy Committee, 2026-10-22, as quoted by Kelly Hammargren: a "5 or 10-year storm" "could result in a 12-foot sea level rise in the waterfront" (M1). Read here as a 12 ft NAVD88 water level (M2, inference). Unconfirmed: its source, its datum, and whether it includes waves. As still water it is above the 500-year level (10.91, W11); FEMA's wave-inclusive flood elevations on the exposed Marina shoreline are 12 to 14 ft (W6), and a still-water fill shows no waves.

scenarios.label: Modeled surface connection behind I-80
scenarios.source: A result of this explorer's terrain model, not a protective threshold. The connected fill first reaches the transfer station and the West Berkeley flats once the level passes 13.35 ft NAVD88, over ground just east of I-80 about 250 m south of Gilman St (tools/overtop.mjs; SOURCE_NOTES C6). The figure is uncertain and the uncertainty is not quantified: lidar error, the 4 m grid, and culverts, ramps and embankments the bare-earth surface misrepresents can each move it, and the crossing needs Caltrans profiles to confirm. The Draft EIR's ART-based maps put the site's first flooding near 13.2 ft NAVD88 (F9); ART's layers at that level, MHHW + 84 in (13.20 ft NAVD88), show the site as disconnected low-lying ground (41% of it), not connected to the Bay; ART's next map, + 96 in (14.20 ft NAVD88), floods 56% of it from the Bay (C6, C20). Those discrete maps bracket the connection without establishing its level.
